entries.title: WebSocket support is now generally available

entries.content:
WebSocket support in Vercel Functions is now generally available.

Since the public beta launched in late June, Vercel CDN has served 300 million WebSocket connections, and now serves 15 million per day.

Customers use WebSockets for AI chat, streaming, and realtime multiplayer apps. WebSockets also power AI Gateway's realtime models.

WebSocket connections follow the same limits and pricing as other Function invocations. With Active CPU pricing, CPU is billed only for the time spent processing messages.

Get started at the documentation.

Contributors

Mark Glagola, Ethan Niser, Casey Gowrie

entries.content:
We are updating the Terms of Service for Hobby and Pro customers, effective October 19, 2026. The updates clarify some existing Vercel practices, expand terms on topics such as managed accounts and credits, and reflect applicable legal requirements, including certain cancellation and service-change rights for eligible consumers in the UK and EU.

Copy link to headingCredits and billing

A new section sets out how credits work: plan-included credits expire at the end of the subscription term and purchased credits expire one year after purchase unless stated otherwise in the relevant credit purchase terms. Credits can only be used to pay Vercel fees, have no cash value, and are nontransferable. Credits are generally nonrefundable, but unused purchased credits are refunded if Vercel terminates your account without cause.

The Terms also clarify that credit purchases are billed in advance, subscriptions auto-renew unless you turn off renewal, and third-party pass-through rates may change when provider rates change. ⁠⁠

Copy link to headingManaged accounts

The Terms now have a dedicated section for accounts that use a company email domain (e.g., work email), clarifying that the company can manage only the Projects you create inside its Team. We also clarified that if your company wishes to manage your account using your company work email, Vercel will now notify you first and give you a reasonable amount of time to move your personal content to an account with a different email address

Copy link to headingRenewal and cancellation

You can turn off auto-renewal and cancel or downgrade through account settings or Support. Cancellation or downgrade generally takes effect at the start of the next renewal period. The Terms also explain statutory withdrawal and refund rights for eligible consumers.

Copy link to headingService changes

Eligible consumers in the UK and EU may cancel the affected subscription free of charge if a change has more than a minor negative impact on their access to or use of the Services. They have 30 days from notice or the change, whichever is later, and may receive a prorated refund of prepaid amounts for the remaining period.

Copy link to headingOther updates

The service-specific provisions have been moved to a dedicated Service Terms page. The Terms also clarify sanctions-related obligations, including that use of the Services must not be in connection with or for the benefit of a sanctioned person under applicable laws.

Read the full Terms of Service and Service Terms for details.

entries.title: Making every harness durable
entries.summary: Developers are familiar with running coding agents locally through harnesses like Pi, Claude Code, and others. entries.content:
Developers are familiar with running coding agents locally through harnesses like Pi, Claude Code, and others. They are reliable daily drivers for generating code, but keeping agents running around the clock requires your computer to be on and awake, which led to the laptop lid memes and Mac mini demand spike.

Copy link to headingRunning harnesses in the cloud

Harness workloads are moving to the cloud. Individual developers are deploying always-on coding agent workflows, projects like OpenWork and HanaAgent use open-source harnesses as the engines behind the apps, and engineers are building their own harness products.

These harnesses are designed for long-lived processes that keep the session in memory, and agent tasks commonly run for minutes or hours. Locally, a harness has direct, continuous access to the workspace and session history on the same disk, so resuming interrupted work only requires a simple prompt.

In the cloud, you can replicate that setup with a VM and persistent storage, but the VM doesn't automatically record which model and tool calls completed or resume interrupted turns after a crash. A failed turn or network error means lost work.

Also, not every agent task executed through a harness needs a sandbox. Database queries and API calls can run securely in functions, and that also means required credentials never have to enter the sandbox.

Copy link to headingMaking every harness durable

We built eve and fx to run durably in the cloud out of the box, and today we are introducing 

durable-harness
, which extends that durability to any harness, including Pi, OpenCode, Codex, and Claude Code. It uses the same machinery that powers Workflow SDK to survive crashes and function timeouts.

With 

durable-harness
, you can:

  • Run any of these harnesses durably on Vercel

  • Self-host a harness with your own Postgres instance

  • Make your local harness workflow durable

  • Build your own durable harness

Copy link to headingSessions that survive a crash mid-turn

Take the example of a coding agent adding a pricing page to an existing app. The agent reads the existing page, writes a new one, opens a pull request, and waits for CI to finish before reporting back.

What happens if its function times out while CI is still running?

Kill the function or drop the connection in the demo below to compare how the two agents recover and which work is repeated.

Without durability, the agent stops work until it is manually restarted, and completed work is repeated unnecessarily.

With 

durable-harness
, a new function reads completed results from the log and resumes the turn. If the browser disconnects, the agent keeps running, and reconnecting catches up from the log.

Copy link to headingLogs and queues

durable-harness
is the newest package in our open source portfolio. It’s a set of adapters and utilities that let the harnesses you already use keep their sessions in a World, the Workflow SDK’s durable backend.

It writes each step of a turn to a durable log. Before a model call or tool call runs, it records an intent, and when the call finishes, it records the outcome. The turn itself is backstopped with a queue message, so if its function dies, the queue hands the turn to a new function that reads the log and continues where it left off.

After a crash, the log says what finished, what was running, and what never started:

  • Completed calls never run again because their results are read from the log, so you’re never billed twice for a finished model call’s tokens.

  • Models remember their previous calls rather than repeating them.

  • Interrupted tools marked 

    replay: 'safe'
    run again. Any other tool comes back to the model as possibly run, and the model decides whether to check.

Harnesses that keep their own session files, like Claude Code's transcript, Codex's rollout, and OpenCode's event store, have every record mirrored into the log, so a new function or Sandbox rebuilds them from it.

Copy link to headingPick your harness

fx and eve are durable on their own. For the rest, 

durable-harness
adds durability from the outside, without changing the harness.

For the full setup guide for each harness, check the docs.

Copy link to headingRuns everywhere

Durable agents need a log of each step, a way to resume a turn when its process dies, and a stream for whoever is watching.

Workflow SDK ships all three behind one interface, a World.

      
import type { Queue, Storage, Streamer } from '@workflow/world'interface World extends Storage, Queue, Streamer {}

A World is the log, the backstop and the stream behind one interface.

durable-harness
writes to that interface, so you can move the same agent from one World to another without changing its code:

  • On Vercel, it uses the Vercel World.

  • In development, it uses files on your machine.

  • On your own servers, it uses Postgres, MongoDB, Redis, or Turso.

Two variables move every agent using 

durable-harness
to Postgres. 
      
WORKFLOW_TARGET_WORLD="@workflow/world-postgres"WORKFLOW_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://user:password@host:5432/database"

Redirects durable-harness to use the Postgres World for durability.

For more control, such as setting a namespace or recovering sessions when your server starts, create the World in code and pass it to your agent:

Check the self-hosting docs for more details.

Copy link to headingSee every session in Agent Runs

Agent Runs on Vercel shows the trace for every session, including each model call and tool call. Turns that resumed after a crash appear in the same trace, so you can see exactly where a turn stopped and picked back up.

A Pi session in the Agent Runs tab with an interrupted and retried model call.

Copy link to headingTools

An agent has only the tools you give it, and they run in your function. Each tool says what should happen if a crash interrupts it. A 

'safe'
tool, such as a lookup, can run again. A 
'never'
tool, such as a refund, never runs twice: the model is told the call may have happened, so it can check before it tries again.

Here’s how the coding agent from the demo above might define its tools:

  • A tool that reads a file or checks CI status is marked as 

    'safe'
    so it can run again automatically.

  • A tool that posts a PR comment is marked as 

    'never'
    so that comments aren't posted twice.

The following example defines a tool for each policy using the example of an agent processing a refund:

      
import { pi } from 'durable-harness/pi';import type { HostTool } from 'durable-harness';import { getOrder, refundOrder } from './orders'; // your own code
const tools: HostTool[] = [  {    name: 'get_order',    description: 'Looks up an order',    replay: 'safe', // safe to run again after a crash    inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id'] },    execute: async ({ id }) => JSON.stringify(await getOrder(id)),  },  {    name: 'refund_order',    description: 'Refunds an order',    replay: 'never', // never runs twice    inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id'] },    execute: async ({ id }) => JSON.stringify(await refundOrder(id)),  },];
export const agent = pi({ model: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5', tools });

A lookup can run again after a crash, and a refund never runs twice.

For each harness’s built-in tools, like its shell and file editing, read on.

Copy link to headingFiles

When a harness needs a shell and files, it’s not safe to run them directly on a shared serverless function host. Many sessions can share the same function, and its filesystem isn’t guaranteed to persist between invocations.

To address this, 

durable-harness
gives you a few options: 

  • virtual()
    keeps the files in the session’s log, with a bash-compatible shell that can’t reach your function’s files or the network. It suits short tasks and small workspaces without starting an entire sandbox. 

  • virtual({ durable: false })
    keeps the files in memory for scratch work and clears them at the end of every turn. 

  • sandbox()
    gives the session its own Vercel Sandbox, with 
    /workspace
    on a Drive that outlives every sandbox and every function. It suits real projects and long-running work.

Compare the three side by side in the docs.

Each harness’s built-in tools run on the workspace you choose. With Pi, 

CodingTools
installs Pi’s own 
read
, 
write
, 
edit
, and 
bash
, and 
virtualEnv()
or 
sandboxEnv()
gives them a workspace: 
      
import { BACKGROUND_CONTEXT as ctx } from '@earendil-works/chord/context';import { createRegistry, Harness, type Storage } from '@earendil-works/pi-durable';import { CodingTools, gatewayModels, resumeWith, virtualEnv } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable';
const models = gatewayModels();const registry = createRegistry();registry.install(CodingTools); // Pi's read, write, edit, and bash
// Files kept in the session's log, or sandboxEnv() for the session's own Vercel Sandboxconst env = virtualEnv();
export const open = resumeWith((storage: Storage) => Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, env }, ctx));

Gives Pi its coding tools on a virtual workspace or in a Vercel Sandbox.

For OpenCode, pass the workspace as 

workspace
, and for fx, pass it to 
fxTools()
. Claude Code and Codex always run in a Vercel Sandbox, since they expect a real shell and filesystem, and aren’t safe for multi-tenant use. Their built-in tools work on the session’s Drive once you turn them on with 
builtins: true
. Each harness guide lists its built-in tools.

Copy link to headingDocuments

Some state belongs with the session but isn’t part of the conversation, such as a to-do list, a plan, or a form the agent fills in. A document is typed JSON that lives in the session’s log, so it survives a crash and moves with the session.

Tools can edit documents through 

io.docs
, and each edit commits to the log alongside the tool’s result, so the document’s durable state stays consistent with the tool calls themselves: 
      
import { defineDoc, type HostTool } from 'durable-harness';
export const Todos = defineDoc<{ items: string[] }>({  kind: 'app.todos',  version: 1,  initial: () => ({ items: [] }),});
export const addTodo: HostTool<{ item: string }> = {  name: 'add_todo',  description: 'Adds a todo',  replay: 'safe',  inputSchema: { type: 'object', properties: { item: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['item'] },  async execute({ item }, io) {    const todos = io.docs!.update(Todos, (draft) => {      draft.items.push(item);    });    return `${todos.items.length} todos`;  },};

Defines a to-do list document and a tool that adds to it.

Your app can read and edit the same document without a database of its own, and the chat route can even stream every change to your UI:

      
import { agent } from '@/lib/agent';import { Todos } from '@/lib/todos';
// In a route or webhook: read the list without a database of your ownconst { value } = await agent.sessions.doc(sessionId, Todos);
// In the chat route: stream every change to the browserexport const { GET, POST } = agent.chatRoute({ authorize, docs: [Todos] }); // your auth check

Reads the to-do list from your app and streams its changes to your UI.

In fact, the 

virtual()
workspace from earlier is built on documents: its file tree is a document in the session’s log, and each tool call’s changes commit with its result.

Learn more about tools, files, and documents and how to keep your agent secure.

Copy link to headingWrapping up

Developers choose a harness for the choices it makes about prompts, tools, and context. How it survives a crash shouldn’t be one of them. With 

durable-harness
, a turn that loses its function partway through continues from the log on a new one, without a manual retry and without repeating what already finished. Self-hosting and portability work out of the box by building on top of the Workflow SDK’s World interface. 

durable-harness
is open source on GitHub.

Make your harness durable

Adapters that make Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex durable on Vercel, Postgres, or your laptop.

Read the docs

entries.content:
Mercury 3 from Inception is now available on AI Gateway with 50% off launch pricing. Inception reports strong results across a range of benchmarks, with generation speeds above 1,000 tokens per second.

Mercury 3 uses diffusion to generate text through parallel refinement. It brings improved reasoning to latency-sensitive workloads such as browser agents, real-time search, interactive education, and customer support. A 1M-token context window gives those applications room for long documents and extended conversation histories.

Set 

AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
in your environment. Use 
inception/mercury-3
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'inception/mercury-3',  prompt: 'Write a brief, friendly reply to a customer whose delivery is late.',});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Then select 

inception/mercury-3
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

Try Mercury 3 in the model playground.

AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more.

AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.

You can view all language models available on AI Gateway.

entries.content:
MiniMax M3.1 Flash from MiniMax is now available on AI Gateway for free until Oct 22.

MiniMax M3.1 Flash is an open-weight multimodal model for coding and agentic work, with a 1M-token context window for long documents and multi-step agent sessions.

Compared with earlier MiniMax models, M3.1 Flash improves on complex agentic tasks, coding, and cybersecurity. On the agent side, that covers multi-step business processes and computer use that carries a task from one application to the next. For coding, MiniMax reports its best results on application development, particularly frontend interactions, targeted bug fixes, and component tests.

The free rate applies only when MiniMax serves the request. To make sure it does, sort the provider with 

order
in the gateway provider options. After the offer ends, pinned requests bill at MiniMax's standard rate.

Call it through the AI SDK, the Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages APIs, or a coding agent connected to AI Gateway. Use 

minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash',  reasoning: 'low',  prompt: 'Write a SQL query that finds duplicate emails in a users table.',});

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Then select 

minimax/minimax-m3.1-flash
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

Try MiniMax M3.1 Flash in the model playground.

Each row shows the coding agent or app that ran the session, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, along with its cost, models, providers, and how much of its input was cached across every turn.Open a session to see its cache hit rate, duration, and path. The path lists each
entries.content:
AI Gateway logs now have a Sessions view that groups requests into sessions and shows how session affinity routed each one. Each row shows the coding agent or app that ran the session, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, along with its cost, models, providers, and how much of its input was cached across every turn.

Open a session to see its cache hit rate, duration, and path. The path lists each turn with its model and timing, and names the provider serving the session along with any earlier ones. Session affinity sends each turn to the provider that served the one before it, so the provider already has most of the prompt in cache. A session that stays on one provider reads more of each prompt from cache.

Filter sessions by turns, client, model, provider, authentication, or cost. Single-turn sessions are hidden until you clear the minimum turns filter.

Session affinity runs by default on text and chat requests. To group requests yourself, send the same 

sessionId
in 
providerOptions.gateway
, or the same 
x-session-id
header, on every request in a conversation. Requests without one are grouped by a fingerprint of the conversation's opening and appear as fingerprinted sessions.

Read the session affinity documentation for more information on how AI Gateway identifies sessions.

entries.content:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is now available on AI Gateway.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash that improves reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and image understanding.

The coding gains show up in terminal work and in building and editing whole repositories, and the agentic gains in multi-step automation. With images, the model reads charts and handles visual reasoning more accurately when it can call tools.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 also finishes tasks faster and with shorter outputs than the previous snapshot, so agent runs tend to take less time and use fewer output tokens.

Use 

deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017',  prompt: 'Write a script that retries failed uploads with exponential backoff.',});

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Try DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 in the model playground.

entries.title: Vercel and Shopify make agents first-class shoppers
entries.summary: Agents already shop on the web, but they often use pages and tools originally built for people and search engines. Building a better shopping experience for agents means treating them as first-class shoppers, with product information they can read directly and tools designed for agents to shop.Today, Vercel Shop, our open source Next.js storefront template for Shopify, is generally available. Team
entries.content:
Agents already shop on the web, but they often use pages and tools originally built for people and search engines. Building a better shopping experience for agents means treating them as first-class shoppers, with product information they can read directly and tools designed for agents to shop.

Today, Vercel Shop, our open source Next.js storefront template for Shopify, is generally available. Teams can launch storefronts optimized for how people, search engines, and agents interact with them.

Vercel Shop is built on Shopify’s Hydrogen SDK. The SDK gives teams access to the store’s product catalog, cart and order management, payments, and checkout to build custom storefronts. Earlier this year, Vercel and Shopify announced plans to rebuild Hydrogen to work across JavaScript frameworks. Today, the rebuilt SDK is generally available.

Checkouts are ridiculously hard to get right. It's one of those pieces of software that actually does need 20 years of tinkering with. And Shopify has always been very open, and so we invite people to remix pieces from our checkout just as much as you want. Basically taking all the infrastructure that Shopify built, and you can build whatever you want with it.Tobias Lütke Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Shopify

Copy link to headingGive agents the information and tools they need

Vercel Shop makes product pages available as machine-readable content, including price, availability, and options. The same product URL can serve a visual page to people or product information that agents can read without interpreting the page’s layout. The template also includes structured data embedded in pages and sitemaps to help search and answer engines discover and understand the products.

Shopify co-developed the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), which gives agents a standard way to search a store’s catalog, read product details, check availability, build a cart, and get a checkout link. Vercel Shop makes these capabilities discoverable at the merchant’s own domain, so agents can use MCP to search products and build carts without navigating the site.

Copy link to headingCustomize the experience for all customers

Vercel Shop brings the store’s product catalog, cart, and checkout together with a Next.js storefront, product information and shopping tools for agents, and a shopping assistant powered by eve. The storefront and assistant live in the same codebase, so teams can customize the store’s design and how the assistant helps shoppers.

Skills included in the template guide coding agents through setup, customization, and template updates. Teams can create an experience where shoppers browse product pages or ask the assistant to find products and add them to their cart. Both share the same cart, so shoppers keep what they’ve added as they move between experiences.

You can build a highly custom, well-designed, agent-ready experience with Vercel Shop. It runs on Next.js, it's built on Shopify, and it's freaking fast.Guillermo Rauch Founder & CEO @ Vercel

Copy link to headingStorefronts built with Shopify and Vercel

Today, we launched our merch store at vercel.store with limited-edition drops. It’s built on Vercel Shop. The store’s shopping agent helps shoppers find products, add them to their cart, and continue to checkout.

Shopify, Next.js, and Vercel already power storefronts for brands including AG1, Bombas, and PAIGE. When PAIGE re-architected its ecommerce platform, it saw a 22% increase in revenue and a 76% increase in conversion over Black Friday and Cyber Monday, with no downtime.

Copy link to headingGet started with Vercel Shop

Create a storefront:

      
pnpm create next-app@latest my-store --example https://github.com/vercel/shop

Get started with Vercel Shop. Check the documentation to connect your Shopify store and configure the storefront.

entries.content:
Glimpse from Elorian is now available on AI Gateway. The visual reasoning model accepts images and video to follow objects through motion, interpret spatial relationships, and connect an action to its physical consequences.

Glimpse can return to visual evidence as it works: zooming into a detail, revisiting a short interval of video, or tracking the same feature across frames. This allows the model to support use cases like scientific chart analysis, video captioning, visual counting, and robotics data annotation.

Some examples include checking a train's motion to determine whether it is slowing down, keeping objects distinct through camera movement, and labeling completed actions in robot footage.

Use 

elorian/glimpse
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'elorian/glimpse',  messages: [{    role: 'user',    content: [      { type: 'text', text: 'Describe this image in one sentence.' },      {        type: 'file',        mediaType: 'image/jpeg',        data: new URL('https://elorian.ai/assets/blog/glimpse/open-pliers.jpg'),      },    ],  }],  maxOutputTokens: 4096,  reasoning: 'low'});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

With AI SDK 7, you can send a video as a file part. Replace the placeholder URL with a public or signed HTTPS URL for your video:

      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'elorian/glimpse',  maxOutputTokens: 4096,  messages: [{    role: 'user',    content: [      { type: 'text', text: 'Describe the visible scene in at most five words. Do not use code or search.' },      {        type: 'file',        data: new URL('https://example.com/your-video.mp4'),        mediaType: 'video/mp4',      },    ],  }],  reasoning: 'low',  providerOptions: { elorian: { video_fps: 1 } }});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

To configure AI Gateway in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Try Glimpse in the model playground.

entries.content:
Perplexity Decider V1.2 27B and Decider Flash V1.2 4B are now available on AI Gateway. Both are multimodal decision models for classifying content, routing requests, and scoring text, structured records, and images.

The models answer typed questions with probabilities. Boolean questions return the likelihood of yes, Choice questions select from categories you define, and Score questions assess content against an ordered rubric. Your application can use those results to route a support ticket, flag a damaged product, or send an uncertain decision for human review. Multiple questions can share the same input in one request.

  • Decider V1.2 27B (

    perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2
    ) is the larger model, for nuanced judgments and detailed rubrics.

  • Decider Flash V1.2 4B (

    perplexity/pplx-decider-flash-v1.2
    ) is the smaller model, for high-volume labeling, filtering, and routing with clear criteria.

The examples below use 

perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2
and check the same delivery report through the AI SDK, the Decisions API, and the TypeSafe-compatible API: 
      
import { experimental_decide as decide } from 'ai';
const result = await decide({  model: 'perplexity/pplx-decider-v1.2',  state: 'The tablet arrived with a shattered display and will not turn on.',  questions: {    damaged: {      type: 'boolean',      instructions: 'Does this report a damaged delivery?',    },  },});
console.log(result.answers.damaged);

For image input, embed base64 

image_url
objects in JSON 
state
through the AI SDK or TypeSafe-compatible API. See Perplexity's image format and the decision models documentation for request formats and question types.

Explore Decider V1.2 27B in the model playground, or try Decider Flash V1.2 4B.

Use AI Gateway to call models with one API key and monitor usage and cost in one place. Decision requests are recorded in request logs and included in spend budgets. Inference uses provider pricing without a markup or platform fee. This also applies when you supply your own provider credentials through BYOK.

Browse the decision model catalog to see the available options.
